transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

What brought me in is, my wife will be telling me about my cousin’s appointments or rides, and I’m looking right at her, but then a minute later I realize I didn’t really take in half of what she said.
About how long have you been experiencing this kind of difficulty paying attention?
It’s been noticeably harder for about 11 months, since my cousin moved in with us after surgery.
Did you experience difficulties with attention or focus when you were growing up, such as during your school years?
Yes. Even in grade school, before I was 12, my teachers would tell my parents I was bright but always daydreaming. I’d leave homework in my desk and needed reminders to finish my classwork.
Do you also notice these difficulties with focus and attention in other areas of your life, such as at work?

I’m not working now, but I notice it with other things. If I sit down to work out a catering order or listen to a parish planning call, I start off fine, but before long my mind wanders. Then I have to go back over the same notes like I never read them.
Do you often feel physically restless or have trouble sitting still without fidgeting?
Not really. I haven’t particularly noticed being physically restless or needing to fidget.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports significant and persistent symptoms of inattention, including mind wandering during conversations, difficulty sustaining focus during tasks, and having to repeatedly re-read material. Symptoms have caused notable impairment for the past 11 months and are present across multiple settings (home and community/parish activities). A childhood onset of inattention prior to age 12 was confirmed, and hyperactive/impulsive symptoms were denied, supporting a diagnosis of attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation (coded under F90.0 in ICD-10).
